Metastases from renal carcinoma are typically lytic, but may appear mixed or sclerotic, for example after therapies (radiotherapy, anti-angiogenic drugs or immunotherapy) that induce reparative sclerosis. A vertebral fracture in an oncologic patient should be considered pathologic until proven otherwise: signs in favor are a focal lesion of the body, pedicle involvement, a convex posterior wall and a soft-tissue component; in favor of osteoporosis are sharp fracture lines, the vacuum phenomenon and normal signal of the residual marrow on MRI.
In the report: level, residual height of the body, posterior wall, fragments in the canal, SINS, other lesions (here T8).
